claim: RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) is frequently used to assess the effect of genetic mutations on cellular and developmental processes in model organisms.
source: In model organisms, RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) is frequently used to assess the effect of genetic mutations on cellular and developmental processes.
evidence: This is a general statement about common practice in the field, drawing from established scientific knowledge.

claim: Animals heterozygous for a mutation are typically crossed to produce offspring with different genotypes for RNA-seq experiments.
source: Typically, animals heterozygous for a mutation are crossed to produce offspring with different genotypes.
evidence: This describes standard experimental practice in the field.

claim: Resultant embryos are grouped by genotype to compare homozygous mutant embryos to heterozygous and wild-type siblings.
source: Resultant embryos are grouped by genotype to compare homozygous mutant embryos to heterozygous and wild-type siblings.
evidence: This describes standard experimental methodology.

claim: Genes that are differentially expressed between genotype groups are assumed to reveal insights into the pathways affected by the mutation.
source: Genes that are differentially expressed between the groups are assumed to reveal insights into the pathways affected by the mutation.
evidence: This describes a common assumption in the interpretation of differential expression experiments.

claim: In zebrafish, differentially expressed genes are often over-represented on the same chromosome as the mutation due to different levels of expression of alleles from different genetic backgrounds.
source: Here we show that in zebrafish, differentially expressed genes are often over-represented on the same chromosome as the mutation due to different levels of expression of alleles from different genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There is evidence of widespread allele-specific expression in zebrafish using an incross of haplotype-resolved wild-type fish.
source: Using an incross of haplotype-resolved wild-type fish, we found evidence of widespread allele-specific expression, which appears as differential expression when comparing embryos homozygous for a region of the genome to their siblings.
evidence: This finding is supported by experimental data from the SAT line incross described in the manuscript.

claim: Allele-specific expression appears as differential expression when comparing embryos homozygous for a region of the genome to their siblings.
source: Using an incross of haplotype-resolved wild-type fish, we found evidence of widespread allele-specific expression, which appears as differential expression when comparing embryos homozygous for a region of the genome to their siblings.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data from the SAT line incross.

claim: The differential expression of genes on the same chromosome as a mutation of interest may not be caused by that mutation when analyzing mutant transcriptomes.
source: When analysing mutant transcriptomes, this means that the differential expression of genes on the same chromosome as a mutation of interest may not be caused by that mutation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing ASE effects.

claim: The genomic location of a differentially expressed gene is typically not considered when interpreting its importance with respect to the phenotype.
source: Typically, the genomic location of a differentially expressed gene is not considered when interpreting its importance with respect to the phenotype.
evidence: This describes current practice in the field.

claim: Spurious differentially expressed genes on the same chromosome as the mutation could lead to pathways being erroneously implicated or overlooked.
source: This could lead to pathways being erroneously implicated or overlooked due to the noise of spurious differentially expressed genes on the same chromosome as the mutation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential consequences of the observed ASE effect.

claim: These observations have implications for the interpretation of RNA-seq experiments involving outbred animals and non-inbred model organisms.
source: These observations have implications for the interpretation of RNA-seq experiments involving outbred animals and non-inbred model organisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Large-scale genetic screens to identify gene function by randomly introducing mutations have been a staple of zebrafish genetics for several decades.
source: Large-scale genetic screens to identify gene function by randomly introducing mutations have been a staple of zebrafish genetics for several decades (Driever et al., 1996; Haffter et al., 1996; Kettleborough et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The advent of RNA-sequencing has enabled investigators to estimate the location of mutations in the genome while also providing information regarding gene expression levels and affected cellular pathways in mutants.
source: The advent of RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) has enabled investigators to estimate the location of such mutations in the genome, while also providing information regarding gene expression levels and affected cellular pathways in the mutants.
evidence: This describes established capabilities of RNA-seq technology.

claim: Bioinformatics pipelines which process RNA-seq data to generate gene expression information focus on transcript abundance, differential splicing, and gene set enrichments.
source: The bioinformatics pipelines which process RNA-seq data to generate gene expression information focus on transcript abundance, differential splicing, and gene set enrichments, and, in general, genomic location is not considered when assessing genes that are differentially expressed (DE) in a mutant context.
evidence: This describes standard bioinformatics approaches.

claim: Genomic location is generally not considered when assessing genes that are differentially expressed in a mutant context.
source: The bioinformatics pipelines which process RNA-seq data to generate gene expression information focus on transcript abundance, differential splicing, and gene set enrichments, and, in general, genomic location is not considered when assessing genes that are differentially expressed (DE) in a mutant context.
evidence: This describes current practice in bioinformatics analysis.

claim: Physical location can impact a gene's likelihood of being differentially expressed in mutant zebrafish.
source: Here, we report that physical location can impact a gene's likelihood of being DE in mutant zebrafish.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Male zebrafish from a laboratory wild-type strain are treated with N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea (ENU) to mutagenise sperm in the typical protocol for introducing random point mutations.
source: In the typical protocol for introducing random point mutations, male zebrafish from a laboratory wild-type strain are treated with N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea (ENU) to mutagenise sperm (Kettleborough et al., 2011; Mullins et al., 1994).
evidence: This describes standard mutagenesis protocols, supported by citations.

claim: The mutagenised fish (G0) are mated with wild-type females to produce F1 offspring, each heterozygous at random novel mutation sites.
source: The mutagenised fish (G0) are mated with wild-type females to produce F1 offspring, each heterozygous at random novel mutation sites.
evidence: This describes standard breeding protocols.

claim: F1 fish are outcrossed with wild types to produce clutches of F2 offspring, which are subsequently incrossed to produce F3 embryos.
source: F1 fish are outcrossed with wild types to produce clutches of F2 offspring, which are subsequently incrossed to produce F3 embryos.
evidence: This describes standard breeding protocols.

claim: F3 clutches contain novel mutations in Mendelian ratios, and in a forward genetics approach are screened for recessive phenotypes of interest which appear in approximately 25% of embryos.
source: The F3 clutches contain the novel mutations in Mendelian ratios, and in a forward genetics approach are screened for recessive phenotypes of interest which appear in approximately 25% of embryos (Mullins et al., 1994).
evidence: This describes standard forward genetics screening, supported by citation.

claim: Mutant embryos are homozygous for a novel allele (the 'causative mutation') and due to genetic linkage, they are likely to be homozygous for alleles physically nearby on the chromosome.
source: Mutant embryos are homozygous for a novel allele (the 'causative mutation') and due to genetic linkage, they are likely to be homozygous for alleles physically nearby on the chromosome.
evidence: This is based on established principles of genetic linkage.

claim: The location encompassing the causative mutation lies in a region which is highly homozygous in mutants, yet heterozygous in siblings, referred to as linkage disequilibrium (LD).
source: The location encompassing the causative mutation therefore lies in a region which is highly homozygous in mutants, yet heterozygous in siblings. This is referred to as linkage disequilibrium (LD).
evidence: This describes the genetic principle of linkage disequilibrium.

claim: The region of high LD can be mapped using high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatics pipelines.
source: The region of high LD can be mapped using high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatics pipelines (Mackay and Schulte-Merker, 2014; Minevich et al., 2012; Obholzer et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to published methods.

claim: Prior mapping efforts involved painstaking genotyping of simple sequence length polymorphisms and genome walks using bacterial or P1 artificial chromosome libraries or subsequently, microarrays.
source: whereas prior efforts involved painstaking genotyping of simple sequence length polymorphisms and genome walks using bacterial or P1 artificial chromosome libraries or subsequently, microarrays (Stickney et al., 2002; Zhang et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published methods.

claim: All mapping processes rely on identification of polymorphic loci throughout the genome.
source: All mapping processes rely on identification of polymorphic loci throughout the genome.
evidence: This describes a fundamental principle of genetic mapping.

claim: Laboratory zebrafish strains have a high degree of intra-strain polymorphism.
source: Laboratory zebrafish strains have a high degree of intra-strain polymorphism (Guryev et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Mapping is aided by the introduction of alleles from other strains.
source: but mapping is aided by the introduction of alleles from other strains.
evidence: This describes a common practice in genetic mapping.

claim: Mutagenised males are often paired with females from a different strain.
source: Thus, mutagenised males are often paired with females from a different strain.
evidence: This describes common experimental practice.

claim: In a mapping cross, alleles in the mutants and siblings are inherited from two different strains.
source: As a result, in a mapping cross, alleles in the mutants and siblings are inherited from two different strains.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the breeding scheme described.

claim: The highly polymorphic nature of zebrafish strains can lead to gene expression differences between mutant and sibling embryos through allele-specific expression (ASE).
source: In this study, we report that the highly polymorphic nature of zebrafish strains can lead to gene expression differences between mutant and sibling embryos through allele-specific expression (ASE).
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: The effect of ASE is well documented across many species, and can be tissue- and condition-specific.
source: The effect of ASE is well documented across many species, and can be tissue- and condition-specific (Ayroles et al., 2009; Doss et al., 2005; Fu et al., 2009; Battle et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2015; Kim-Hellmuth et al., 2020; Storey et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: ASE manifests as a cluster of DE genes located near to the causative mutation site in many different unrelated mutant lines.
source: Here, this phenomenon manifests as a cluster of DE genes located near to the causative mutation site in many different unrelated mutant lines.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The differential transcript levels of local genes are likely due to expression differences between wild-type strains rather than altered transcription due to the mutation.
source: The differential transcript levels of these local genes are likely due to expression differences between wild-type strains rather than altered transcription due to the mutation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: The high prevalence of ASE in zebrafish is confirmed in the SAT line which is derived from only two haplotypes.
source: We confirm the high prevalence of ASE in zebrafish in the SAT line which is derived from only two haplotypes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the SAT line incross.

claim: Local genes may be a red herring for researchers attempting to use differential expression to explain phenotypes of interest.
source: This observation has implications for researchers attempting to use differential expression to explain phenotypes of interest, not only in zebrafish, but also in other outbred model organisms, as these local genes may simply be a red herring.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the implications of the findings.

claim: RNA-seq and LD mapping based on Cloudmap was used to map the causal mutations for a number of different mutants from forward genetic screens.
source: To map the causal mutations for a number of different mutants from forward genetic screens, we used RNA-seq and LD mapping, based on Cloudmap (Minevich et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the methods used in the study, supported by citation.

claim: A high degree of LD was observed on chromosome 7 at approximately 22 Mbp in the mutant line u426, suggesting the phenotype-causing mutation is near this position.
source: A representative LD mapping plot (taken from the mutant line u426) is shown in Figure 1. We observed a high degree of LD on chromosome 7 at approximately 22 Mbp, suggesting the phenotype-causing mutation is near this position.
evidence: This is supported by the LD mapping data shown in Figure 1.

claim: DESeq2 reported 209 genes as DE (adjusted p-value < 0.05) between mutants and siblings in the u426 line.
source: DESeq2 reported 209 genes as DE (adjusted p-value < 0.05) between mutants and siblings.
evidence: This is a direct result from the DESeq2 analysis.

claim: 15 DE genes were found in a 20 Mbp window centred on the mapping peak at 22 Mbp in the u426 line, representing 7% of all DE genes.
source: Indeed, we found 15 DE genes in an arbitrarily sized 20 Mbp window centred on the mapping peak at 22 Mbp, representing 7% of all DE genes.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: A 20 Mbp window randomly sampled from the zebrafish genome contains approximately 1.4% of known genes.
source: For comparison, a 20 Mbp window randomly sampled (1000 iterations) from the zebrafish genome contains approximately 1.4% of known genes.
evidence: This is a result from computational analysis of the genome.

claim: Of nine mutant lines analysed, seven samples showed a significant, positive effect of LD on the probability of a gene being DE (Benjamini/Hochberg adjusted p-value < 0.05).
source: Of nine mutant lines analysed (Supplementary file 1), seven samples showed a significant, positive effect of LD (Benjamini/Hochberg adjusted p-value < 0.05).
evidence: This is a result from the logistic regression analysis, as shown in Table 1.

claim: In the nl14 sample, the likelihood of finding a DE gene near to the mutation site was over 100-fold higher than the likelihood of finding one at a random other location in the genome.
source: In the most extreme case (the sample nl14), the likelihood of finding a DE gene near to the mutation site was over 100-fold higher than the likelihood of finding one at a random other location in the genome.
evidence: This is based on the odds ratio calculated from the logistic regression analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Comparing mitfaw2/w2 embryos to siblings produces 116 DE genes, 48 of which are present on chromosome 6, which is the chromosome where mitfa is located.
source: For example, comparing mitfaw2/w2 embryos to siblings produces 116 DE genes, 48 of which are present on chromosome 6, which is the chromosome where mitfa is located (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a specific result from the differential expression analysis, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 60 chromosomes from 37 lines had a statistically significant enrichment of DE genes (binomial test, Bonferroni adjusted p < 0.05).
source: In all, 60 chromosomes from 37 lines had a statistically significant enrichment of the DE genes (binomial test, Bonferroni adjusted p < 0.05).
evidence: This is a result from statistical testing of the DeTCT sequencing experiments.

claim: Of the 60 chromosomes with enrichment of DE genes, 44 were on the chromosome carrying the mutation being investigated in the experiment.
source: Of these, 44 were on the chromosome carrying the mutation being investigated in the experiment (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a result from the statistical analysis of the DeTCT experiments.

claim: Of the 16 chromosomes with enrichment not on the mutant chromosome, 7 had an enrichment on chromosome 9, driven by expression of γ-crystallin genes.
source: Of the other 16, 7 had an enrichment on chromosome 9. This was driven by expression of γ-crystallin genes (Supplementary file 3), which are expressed in the lens and present in a cluster on chromosome 9 (Greiling et al., 2009) that we have previously observed as being co-regulated (White et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis, supported by citations to published literature.

claim: γ-crystallin genes are expressed in the lens and present in a cluster on chromosome 9.
source: This was driven by expression of γ-crystallin genes (Supplementary file 3), which are expressed in the lens and present in a cluster on chromosome 9 (Greiling et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The enrichment of γ-crystallin genes on chromosome 9 suggests that the eyes are affected in some of the analysed mutants.
source: This suggests that the eyes are affected in some of the analysed mutants.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of crystallin gene expression.

claim: Whether there was an enrichment of DE genes on the mutant chromosome did not depend on the total number of DE genes found in the experiment.
source: Whether there was an enrichment of DE genes on the mutant chromosome did not depend on the total number of DE genes found in the experiment, although experiments with very high numbers of DE genes tended not to show an enrichment (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Experiments with very high numbers of DE genes tended not to show an enrichment on the mutant chromosome.
source: Whether there was an enrichment of DE genes on the mutant chromosome did not depend on the total number of DE genes found in the experiment, although experiments with very high numbers of DE genes tended not to show an enrichment (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In an intercross of two different sox10 alleles (t3 and baz1), the differential expression of some genes was linked to one of the wild-type chromosomes in the experiment.
source: In one experiment, we noticed that the differential expression of some genes was linked to one of the wild-type chromosomes in the experiment. This experiment was an intercross of two different sox10 alleles, t3 (Dutton et al., 2001) and baz1 (Carney et al., 2006) sampled at 24 hr post-fertilisation (hpf).
evidence: This is an observation from the sox10 compound heterozygote experiment, supported by citations.

claim: Two of the genotypes in the sox10 t3/baz1 cross had expression levels for some genes on the same chromosome as sox10 that were different from the other two genotypes.
source: We noticed that two of the genotypes had expression levels for some genes on the same chromosome as sox10 that were different from the other two genotypes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The groups with higher expression of si:ch73–308m11.1 shared the wild-type chromosome from the baz1/+ parent.
source: The groups with higher expression shared the wild-type chromosome from the baz1/+ parent (Figure 2C, yellow chromosome) whereas the others shared the chromosome carrying the baz1 allele (Figure 2C, blue chromosome).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There is higher expression from the si:ch73–308m11.1 allele on the wild-type chromosome from the baz1/+ parent.
source: One explanation for this is that there is higher expression from the si:ch73–308m11.1 allele on the wild-type chromosome (Figure 2C, yellow chromosome)
evidence: This is an inference from the expression pattern observed in Figure 2C.

claim: The enrichment of DE genes on the mutant chromosome is not necessarily dependent on the mutant gene.
source: which led us to hypothesise that the enrichment of DE genes on the mutant chromosome is not necessarily dependent on the mutant gene.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observations from the sox10 experiment.

claim: ASE (polymorphism-driven variation in expression levels of genes) is common across the genome.
source: Our hypothesis is that ASE, that is, polymorphism-driven variation in expression levels of genes, is common across the genome.
evidence: This is the hypothesis being tested in the study.

claim: The SAT line was generated from an intercross of one fully sequenced double haploid AB fish and one fully sequenced double haploid Tübingen fish.
source: We used the SAT line, which was generated from an intercross of one fully sequenced double haploid AB fish and one fully sequenced double haploid Tübingen fish (Howe et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the origin of the SAT line, supported by citation.

claim: For any position in the SAT line genome there are up to two possible alleles.
source: This means that for any position in the genome there are up to two possible alleles.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the SAT line being derived from two double haploid fish.

claim: The original haplotypes in the SAT line have recombined through the generations that the SAT line has been maintained by incrossing.
source: The original haplotypes have recombined through the generations that the SAT line has been maintained by incrossing.
evidence: This is a statement about the genetic history of the SAT line.

claim: 96 morphologically normal embryos were collected at 5 days post-fertilisation from a SAT incross for RNA-seq.
source: We incrossed two SAT fish, fin-clipped them to isolate DNA for exome sequencing, collected 96 morphologically normal embryos at 5 days post-fertilisation (dpf), extracted RNA from the individual embryos, and did RNA-seq on the 96 samples.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Exome sequencing of the SAT parent fish was used to call SNPs and identify regions that are either homozygous for the AB haplotype, homozygous for the Tübingen haplotype, or heterozygous.
source: We used the exome sequence of the SAT parent fish for this cross to call SNPs and identify regions that are either homozygous for the AB haplotype, homozygous for the Tübingen haplotype, or heterozygous.
evidence: This describes the methods used to identify parental haplotypes.

claim: RNA-seq reads and SNPs identified in the parental exome data were used to genotype the embryos at locations that distinguish the AB and Tübingen haplotypes.
source: Using the RNA-seq reads and SNPs identified in the parental exome data, we genotyped the embryos at locations that distinguish the AB and Tübingen haplotypes.
evidence: This describes the methods used to genotype the embryos.

claim: Aggregating genotype data in 1 Mbp regions allowed determination of the haplotypes of each individual embryo.
source: Aggregating these data in 1 Mbp regions allowed us to determine the haplotypes of each individual embryo.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach used.

claim: 82 different groupings of embryos according to local genotype were identified across the genome.
source: Across the genome, this resulted in 82 different groupings of embryos according to local genotype.
evidence: This is a result from the haplotype analysis.

claim: Differential gene expression analysis on each different embryo grouping revealed DE genes located in or close to the region of the genome that was used to define the embryo groups.
source: Differential gene expression analysis on each different embryo grouping revealed DE genes located in or close to the region of the genome that was used to define the embryo groups (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a result from the differential expression analysis, shown in Figure 3.

claim: The log2(fold changes) of affected genes varied widely but had an absolute mean of 0.5 for the homozygous versus homozygous comparison.
source: The log2(fold changes) of affected genes varied widely but had an absolute mean of 0.5 for the homozygous versus homozygous comparison (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Genes can show ASE in a wild-type context.
source: This demonstrates that genes can show ASE in a wild-type context (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the SAT line experiment, shown in Figure 3.

claim: It was possible to see the consequences of meiotic recombination in individual embryos through the analyses.
source: Through these analyses, it was also possible to see the consequences of meiotic recombination in individual embryos (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Two samples (C7 and E5) showed recombination in the 31–37 Mbp region of chromosome 5.
source: For example, two samples (C7 and E5) showed recombination in the 31–37 Mbp region of chromosome 5 (red ovals in Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an observation from the haplotype data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The genotypes near the myhc4 gene in samples C7 and E5 were the opposite of that called for the whole region, and this is evident in the count plot.
source: The genotypes near the myhc4 gene were the opposite of that called for the whole region and this is evident in the count plot – C7 has expression comparable with the Tu/Tu haplotype, despite being assigned AB/Tu, and E5 has expression similar to the AB/Tu samples despite being assigned Tu/Tu based on the entire 31–37 Mbp region (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: ASE could affect enriched GO terms, but this effect was very variable.
source: These analyses showed that ASE could affect enriched GO terms, but that this effect was very variable (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a result from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Experiments where there wasn't an enrichment of DE genes on the mutant chromosome generally did not show as large an effect on GO terms.
source: Experiments where there wasn't an enrichment of DE genes on the mutant chromosome generally did not show as large an effect, which again makes sense as the DE genes linked to the mutation were a smaller fraction of the gene list.
evidence: This is an observation from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Experiments with fewer DE genes showed larger effects on GO term overlap.
source: Overall, experiments with fewer DE genes showed larger effects.
evidence: This is an observation from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In a sox10 t3/baz1 intercross at 36 hpf, 302 genes were DE, 32 of which were on chromosome 3.
source: For example, in a sox10 t3/baz1 intercross at 36 hpf, 302 genes were DE, 32 of which were on chromosome 3 (the same chromosome as sox10).
evidence: This is a specific result from the differential expression analysis.

claim: GO term enrichment using the full list of genes in the sox10 t3/baz1 intercross produced 92 enriched GO terms, only 49 of which were also enriched if the genes on chromosome 3 had been removed from the list.
source: GO term enrichment using the full list of genes produced 92 enriched GO terms, only 49 of which were also enriched if the genes on chromosome 3 had been removed from the list (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is a result from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: 28 extra GO terms were enriched using the shorter gene list (with chromosome 3 genes removed) in the sox10 t3/baz1 intercross.
source: In addition, 28 extra GO terms were enriched using the shorter gene list.
evidence: This is a result from the GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Genes that were DE between sox10t3/baz1 individuals and their siblings and located on chromosome 3 fell into different groups with respect to their expression levels across the four different genotypes.
source: We went back to the expression data from the compound heterozygous sox10t3;sox10baz1 cross and found that the genes that were DE between sox10t3/baz1 individuals and their siblings and located on chromosome 3 fell into different groups with respect to their expression levels across the four different genotypes (Figure 5).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Ten genes on chromosome 3 showed expression patterns where increased expression was linked to the presence of a specific allele.
source: Ten genes showed expression patterns as shown in Figure 2C, where increased expression was linked to the presence of a specific allele (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the sox10 compound heterozygote data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Only one gene (ENSDARG00000110416) located on another chromosome, encoding an miRNA, showed a similar pattern to the ASE genes on chromosome 3.
source: Only one gene (ENSDARG00000110416) located on another chromosome, encoding an miRNA, showed a similar pattern (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: 15 DE genes (excluding sox10 itself) on chromosome 3 showed genotype-dependent transcript levels consistent with a response to loss of sox10 function.
source: By contrast, the other 15 DE genes (excluding sox10 itself) on chromosome 3 showed genotype-dependent transcript levels that were consistent with (though do not prove) a response to loss of sox10 function, that is, the wild types and the compound heterozygous individuals had opposing expression levels whereas both heterozygous genotypes had intermediate levels or the same as wild types (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Sox10 is a key regulator of neural crest development.
source: Sox10 is a key regulator of neural crest development
evidence: This is established knowledge about sox10 function.

claim: Of the genes speculated to be downstream of sox10, all four with data on ZFIN are expressed in neural (kctd13 and cygb1) and neural crest (syngr1a and vasnb) derivatives.
source: Of the genes we speculated to be downstream of sox10, all four with data on ZFIN are expressed in neural (kctd13 and cygb1) and neural crest (syngr1a and vasnb) derivatives
evidence: This is based on published spatial expression data from ZFIN.

claim: The three ASE candidates with available data on ZFIN (traf7, polr3h, and polr2f) are not spatially restricted.
source: whereas the three ASE candidates with available data are not spatially restricted (traf7, polr3h, and polr2f).
evidence: This is based on published spatial expression data from ZFIN.

claim: For genes showing single allele-linked expression patterns, it is likely that ASE is the primary driver of their differential expression and that they are probably red herrings.
source: Consequently, for genes showing single allele-linked expression patterns, it is likely that ASE is the primary driver of their differential expression and that they are probably red herrings.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of expression patterns.

claim: In 51 out of 124 transcriptional profiling experiments comparing zebrafish mutants and siblings at different stages of development, a statistically significant enrichment of DE genes on the same chromosome as the mutated gene was found.
source: In 51 out of 124 transcriptional profiling experiments comparing zebrafish mutants and siblings at different stages of development, we found a statistically significant enrichment of DE genes on the same chromosome as the mutated gene.
evidence: This is a summary result from the analysis of DeTCT experiments.

claim: In a previous study using RNA-seq to map ENU mutations, very few genes were detected as being DE in regions linked to the mutation.
source: In a previous study using RNA-seq to map ENU mutations (Miller et al., 2013), it was noted that very few genes were detected as being DE in regions linked to the mutation.
evidence: This is a statement about findings from a cited study.

claim: The difference between the current study and Miller et al. is likely the result of methodological differences, the most significant of which is the sample size.
source: This difference is likely the result of methodological differences between the two studies, the most significant of which is the sample size. Miller et al. used one mutant and one wild-type sample, whereas our study has a median sample size of 10 per condition.
evidence: This is a speculation about the reasons for different findings.

claim: The physical arrangement of genes in an organism's genome is not random.
source: The physical arrangement of genes in an organism's genome is not random.
evidence: This is established knowledge in genomics.

claim: Co-expression of functionally related genes using shared regulatory elements and/or transcription factors provides an evolutionary pressure to keep these genes clustered in physical proximity within a chromosome.
source: Co-expression of functionally related genes using shared regulatory elements and/or transcription factors provides an evolutionary pressure to keep these genes clustered in physical proximity within a chromosome (Thévenin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: It is possible that a mutation affecting one gene could alter expression levels of nearby genes if they form a functionally related cluster.
source: Consequently, it is possible that a mutation affecting one gene could alter expression levels of nearby genes if they form a functionally related cluster.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the principle of gene clustering.

claim: The neighbouring DE genes in the tested mutant lines showed no obvious functional connections.
source: However, the neighbouring DE genes in the tested mutant lines showed no obvious functional connections.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of the mutant lines.

claim: 7/16 chromosomal enrichments that were not linked to the mutated genes affected a chromosome 9 cluster of crystallin genes that are expressed in the eye.
source: Of note, 7/16 chromosomal enrichments that were not linked to the mutated genes affected a chromosome 9 cluster of crystallin genes that are expressed in the eye.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of chromosomal enrichments.

claim: The enrichments of DE genes on mutant chromosomes were driven by ASE, which has been widely demonstrated across different tissues and organisms.
source: Instead we found that the enrichments were driven by ASE, which has been widely demonstrated across different tissues and organisms (Battle et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2015; Kim-Hellmuth et al., 2020)
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study, supported by citations to published literature.

claim: ASE can play a role in developmental and disease processes.
source: and can play a role in developmental and disease processes (Libioulle et al., 2007; Moffatt et al., 2007; Nicolae et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: ASE is often tissue-dependent and the average log2(fold change) between alleles in human ASE is about 0.6 as measured in different tissues.
source: ASE is often tissue-dependent and the average log2(fold change) between alleles in human ASE is about 0.6 as measured in different tissues (Battle et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: ASE was observed at similar magnitudes in zebrafish even when averaged across all tissues through whole embryo RNA-seq.
source: Here, we have observed ASE at similar magnitudes even when averaged across all tissues through whole embryo RNA-seq.
evidence: This is a result from the SAT line experiment.
